references.text: Jesus teaches that whoever is faithful in small things is also faithful in great things – the same principle as the reward in the parable of the minas ([ref:Luk 16:10|Luke 16:10]).

In the parable of the talents, the Lord says: "Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much" – a clear parallel to the reward in Luke 19:17 ([ref:Matt 25:21|Matthew 25:21]).
The second servant in Matthew's parable of the talents also receives the same praise and reward for faithfulness over little ([ref:Matt 25:23|Matthew 25:23]).

In the message to the church in Thyatira, the one who conquers and holds fast to Jesus' works is promised power over the nations – faithfulness is rewarded with authority ([ref:Åp 2:26|Revelation 2:26]).
The one who conquers will sit with Christ on his throne – a promise of sharing in his rule, parallel to ruling over cities ([ref:Åp 3:21|Revelation 3:21]).
Paul writes that if we endure, we will also reign with Christ – faithfulness leads to co-regency ([ref:2 Tim 2:12|2 Timothy 2:12]).
Stewards are required to be faithful – the same requirement that underlies the reward in the parable of the minas ([ref:1 Kor 4:2|1 Corinthians 4:2]).
Jesus says that the faithful and wise steward will be put in charge of all his master's possessions – faithfulness in small things leads to greater responsibility ([ref:Luk 12:44|Luke 12:44]).

Jesus promises the disciples a kingdom and that they will sit on thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel – reward with authority for those who have been faithful ([ref:Luk 22:29-30|Luke 22:29-30]).
Daniel prophesies that the kingdom, dominion, and power under heaven will be given to the holy people of the Most High – God's faithful servants receive rule ([ref:Dan 7:27|Daniel 7:27]).
